question: What are the design features and operational parameters of high-temperature and low-temperature plasma reactors used for reactive nitrogen species production?
answer: High-temperature (HT) and low-temperature (LT) plasma reactors for reactive nitrogen species production feature distinct designs and operational parameters. The HT reactor employs a double concentric glass/quartz tube dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) configuration with a central wire electrode (φ 0.5 mm) and grounded outer pipe (OD 9.5 mm), operating at 13.6 kVp-p, 12.5 kHz with 44 W discharge power to generate NOx at ~2000 K adiabatic temperature. The LT reactor uses a standard DBD geometry operating at lower power (3.4 W, 7.8 kVp-p, 5.7 kHz) to maximize O3 yield while minimizing nitrogen dissociation. Both reactors process air at 1 L/min flow rate, with the HT reactor incorporating countercurrent heat exchange for thermal management and the LT reactor optimized for heat dissipation. The systems demonstrate stable operation for 6+ hours with repeatability over 6 months.
